Like other texts in this genre, it recounts the spiritual biography and past karmic merit of a senior monk (*thera*), specifically focusing on the past offering of plantain or banana fruit (*kadaliphala*). SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages for this text [SuttaCentral].

In addition, the text shares extensive formulaic verses with numerous other *apadāna*s centered on fruit offerings, such as the *Mātuluṅgaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 508), the *Panasaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 390), the *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 386), and the *Tālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 511), particularly across repetitive structural segments such as §2.3–8.1 and §3.1–8.1 [DharmaNexus].
